images.note: Real GitHub screenshot from the official 'About commits' doc, showing a commit's page on GitHub with the branch label (main) it was pushed to — i.e., what a real git push actually produces on GitHub.

imageNote: Checked docs.github.com's 'Pushing commits to a remote repository' page via a Browser img.src scan — it renders zero images (push/pull/fetch are terminal-only operations, so GitHub's own doc for them is text-and-code only). The one real screenshot used here (from 'About commits') shows the actual GitHub-side result of a push. The push vs. pull vs. fetch distinction itself — the core teaching point of this lesson — has no GitHub UI counterpart at all, so it's covered with an original LTV steps diagram, documented honestly rather than dressed up as a screenshot.
